title: The printing press was never invented
premise: In 1440 Gutenberg's workshop fails and movable type never spreads. Books remain rare handwritten treasures, and powerful guilds of scribes and memorizers become the keepers of knowledge. Cities learn to speak, paint and remember together, building halls for recitation where libraries would have stood.

chain.event: In Mainz Gutenberg's press trials produce uneven type and lose funding, and movable type is set aside.
chain.consequence: Hand copying remains the only way to make books, keeping them costly and guarded by workshops.

chain.event: Cities charter powerful guilds of scribes and memorizers to license copying and public recitation.
chain.consequence: Scriptoria and recitation halls become civic centers and memory training becomes a honored craft.

chain.event: Teachers develop standard memory halls and picture-sign codes for law, craft and news.
chain.consequence: Ideas travel by trained reciters and painted image boards, allowing shared culture without printed text.

chain.event: Artisans perfect large stencil and relief presses that print pictures, seals and color patterns but not small text.
chain.consequence: Streets fill with vivid image posters and signboards while words stay handwritten, strengthening visual storytelling.

chain.event: Municipal Living Libraries open where citizens can consult reciters and copyists by the hour.
chain.consequence: Oral learning and hand copying become everyday public life, shaping schools, plazas and street architecture.

chain.event: The Concord of Reciters links cities by traveling memory festivals and illuminated public panels.
chain.consequence: Handmade knowledge culture stays vibrant and peaceful, honored in calm gathering places and glowing picture walls.

eras.caption: 1526 · Hall of Copied Voices
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1526. Low timber-and-plaster guild halls with steep thatched roofs stand on the same footprints, their facades wrapped in hand-painted story friezes and hanging wooden scribe signs. Apprentices copy at oak benches in the arcade while neighbours listen in circles under soft golden morning light.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A snug candle-lit copying room with long oak tables, stacked vellum, ink bowls and quills, where robed scribes write quietly side by side.

fossil.brief: Front-facing plaster mural showing a central ring of seated scribes in deep blue robes, left side tall wooden memory shelves stacked with scrolls, right side a flight of white songbirds over a sunlit square. No letters, no words, no text of any kind.

elements.name: ring of seated scribes
elements.explanation: Robed experts signal trusted knowledge worth remembering.

elements.name: tall wooden memory shelves
elements.explanation: Full shelves imply abundance and security through the guild.

elements.name: flight of white songbirds
elements.explanation: Birds link memory to freedom and gentle uplift.

eras.caption: 1926 · City of Reciters
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1926. Grand brick-and-stone recitation houses with tiled roofs and carved wooden balconies stand on the same footprints, their walls covered in large painted picture panels and enamel seal plaques. Crowds in festival cloaks gather calmly to hear reciters on stepped platforms in clear midday sun.

Families and elders share books and listen to storytellers on woven mats in gentle afternoon light.

eras.caption: 3026 · Garden of Kept Stories
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 3026. Moss-softened limestone arcades and cedar pavilions stand on the same footprints, their roofs and balconies embraced by recitation trees, flowering vines and tended herb gardens. Neighbours walk garden paths and read together in dappled green daylight filtering through leaves.
